name: Genetic Neurovascular Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of first-degree relative with confirmed neurovascular malformation
Neurovascular malformation confirmed by MRI, MRA, or angiography
Identification of pathogenic variant in associated neurovascular malformation gene
Presence of neurological symptoms attributable to vascular malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including imaging confirmation and family history or genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Direct abnormal connection between arteries and veins in the brain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracranial hemorrhage due to vascular malformation rupture
pathognomonic.notes: Sudden bleeding within the brain caused by vessel rupture
searchTerms: brain bleeding from blood vessel rupture
intracranial hemorrhage due to vascular malformation

common.notes: Epileptic events triggered by abnormal vascular structures
searchTerms: seizures caused by blood vessel lesions
brain seizures linked to vascular problems

common.notes: Localized weakness or sensory loss related to lesion location
Chronic or episodic headaches linked to vascular abnormalities
searchTerms: headaches linked to blood vessel malformations

common.notes: Visible skin telangiectasias or capillary malformations

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate deficits in memory or executive function
Temporary neurological symptoms due to vascular insufficiency
Nosebleeds caused by fragile nasal mucosal vessels
searchTerms: epistaxis related to blood vessel issues

occasional.notes: Blurred vision or visual field defects from vascular lesions

rare.notes: Abnormal vessels affecting spinal cord function
searchTerms: abnormal blood vessels in spinal cord

rare.notes: Weakness on one side of the body from lesion impact
searchTerms: weakness on one side of body from vascular lesion
hemiparesis due to blood vessel problem

rare.notes: Abnormal lung blood vessel connections causing hypoxemia

laboratory: Possible elevated inflammatory markers if hemorrhage present
imaging: Digital subtraction angiography confirming vascular anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as RASA1, ENG, or ACVRL1

distinguishingFeatures: Familial forms linked to CCM1, CCM2, CCM3 genes

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with neurological deficit
